Map studio & Map studio for dashboards

Nine layer types, one layer or many

Both extensions share the same layer types. The viz extension draws one layer per sheet; the dashboard extension stacks several.

Map extensions
Why

What native Tableau maps don't do easily

The extensions fill the gaps, while everything stays a normal Tableau sheet that responds to filters, actions and parameters.

Map types beyond the Marks card

  • Hex bins, 3D bars, cartograms (area = a measure)
  • Tracks: one path per storm / vehicle through time
  • Flow arcs and pie charts as symbols
  • Density heat map, shapefile polygons and lines

A real second dimension

  • Flat map or 3D globe, with auto-rotate
  • Built-in time line with play button
  • Several layers stacked in one map
  • No map service: the base map ships with the extension

Built for authors and viewers

  • Authors set up layers, fields and start view
  • Viewers only see a light "Map" card
  • Settings are saved inside the workbook

Stays Tableau

  • Any filter, dashboard action or parameter changes the rows the extension receives
  • Works with published sources and shapefiles
Map extensions
Overview

The three extensions

Pick by how many layers you need and where the data comes from.

Worksheet extension

Map studio

One sheet = one layer. Added from the sheet's Marks card, it reads the fields on the Marks tiles: Location, Destination, Size, Color, with a spatial field on Detail.

Best for: a single, quick map; one data source.

map-studio.trex
Dashboard extension

Map studio for dashboards

One sheet per layer. Added as an Extension object on a dashboard, it stacks many layers, each read from its own sheet, so each can have a different data source and its own filters.

Best for: shapefile + CSV + published source in one map.

map-studio-dashboard.trex
Dashboard extension

Parameter player

Plays a list parameter like a filter player: play, pause, previous, next, speed and loop. Drives anything tied to the parameter, including every layer of a map at once.

Best for: automatic date / year animation.

parameter-player.trex

Map extensions
Key concept

Two setting cards: one for everyone, one for the author

The extension asks Tableau whether you are authoring or viewing, and shows each audience only what it needs.

Authoring: Layer setup + Map cards
Viewing: only the Map card

Layer setup (authoring only)

Layer type, fields, time field, start view, measure-name parameter, add / reorder layers. Hidden when the workbook is viewed; saved in the workbook.

Map (everyone)

Flat or globe, dark or light, base map, time line, layers on/off, legend, palette, opacity. A viewer's choices last for the session only.

Map studio for dashboards

One sheet per layer

Each layer reads its own worksheet, so layers can use different data sources and different filters.

Sheet "Regions"
GeometrySales
Shapefile source · filter: State
Sheet "Stores"
LongitudeLatitudeRevenue
CSV source · filter: Format
Sheet "Routes"
OriginDestinationFlights
Published source · filter: Year
➜
Three layers (Countries, Peaks, Flights), each from its own sheet
Fields must be on each sheet's Detail (a layer only sees the fields in its sheet's view). Sheets can be small, floating or hidden, and still return data. One layer is created automatically for every sheet that has map fields.
Map extensions
Parameter player

Plays a parameter, so the whole dashboard animates

Tableau has no play button for parameters. This extension adds one.

  • Controls: first, previous, play / pause, next, scrub bar
  • Speed (slow to very fast) and Loop
  • Gear icon chooses the parameter; the choice is saved in the workbook
  • Follows the parameter if someone changes it by hand

How it fits a map

The parameter drives a filter or calculation in each layer's sheet, so one press of play steps all the layers through time together.

Requirement: a parameter with a list of allowable values (e.g. years, month labels, dates formatted as text).

Alternative for one layer: give the layer a Time field in Layer setup and use the extension's own play bar. The player is the choice when several sheets must move together.
Map extensions
Getting started

Install in two minutes

Hosted on GitHub Pages, so nothing to run locally.

  1. Download the three .trex files from the repo mpsailamarc/tableau-map-extensions (folders map-studio, map-studio-dashboard, parameter-player).
  2. In Desktop: Marks card ▸ Add Extension ▸ Access Local Extensions for Map studio; Dashboard ▸ Extension object ▸ Access Local Extensions for the other two.
  3. Allow the extension to access the data when Tableau asks.

Tableau Cloud / Server

The URL must be HTTPS and a site admin must allow-list it (Settings ▸ Extensions):

https://mpsailamarc.github.io/tableau-map-extensions/

Good to know

  • Settings travel with the workbook
  • Use Save & fetch latest in Layer setup to pull updates, then Tableau's Reload
  • The repository holds no data, only code

User guide

Build a map

Part A · One layer

Map studio on a single sheet, including a measure swapper.

Part B · Several layers

Map studio for dashboards, a parameter that changes the date, and a filter per layer.

User guide A · one layer

A single-layer map in six steps

Example: sales by store as symbols on a globe.

  1. Connect the data. Use longitude / latitude, or a shapefile (its Geometry field).
  2. New sheet ▸ Marks card ▸ Add Extension ▸ Map studio.
  3. Drag fields onto the tiles: Location (place name), Size, Color. A spatial field goes on Detail.
  4. Open Layer setup: pick the type (shapes, symbols, hex bins…), check the fields, optionally a Time field.
  1. Use the Map card: flat or globe, dark or light, palette, legend. Pan and zoom, then Use current view as start.
  2. Place the sheet on a dashboard, add filters, save. Viewers see only the Map card.
Longitude and latitude: right-click the field and choose Convert to Dimension (or use AVG), otherwise SUM adds up repeated rows.
With only place names, countries (name or ISO3) and about 120 major cities are recognised automatically.
Map extensions
User guide A · the non-trivial option

Single layer with a measure swapper

One parameter lets viewers switch the measure the map shows, and the legend and tooltips follow.

  1. Create a string parameter Measure to Display with a list: Sales, Profit, Units.
  2. Create a calculated field Selected Measure:
    CASE [Measure to Display] WHEN 'Sales' THEN SUM([Sales]) WHEN 'Profit' THEN SUM([Profit]) ELSE SUM([Units]) END
  3. Put Selected Measure on Size (and/or Color) of the Map studio sheet.
  4. Show the parameter control on the dashboard.

The non-trivial step

Without help, the legend and tooltips would say AGG(Selected Measure). In Layer setup, set Name the measure from parameter to Measure to Display.

Result

When the viewer picks Profit, the marks resize and the legend and tooltip read "Profit". The setting is available only in the authoring card, so viewers cannot break it.

Map extensions
User guide B · several layers

A multi-layer map with the dashboard extension

Example: regions (shapefile) + stores (CSV) + routes (published source).

  1. Build one normal sheet per layer, each on its own data source.
  2. Put every field the layer needs on Detail: Geometry, or longitude + latitude, or origin + destination, plus a measure for size or width.
  3. Create a dashboard. Add the sheets (they may be small, floating or hidden).
  4. Add an Extension object ▸ Map studio for dashboards.
  1. A layer is created automatically for each sheet with map fields. Open Layer setup to choose a different sheet, type, fields or palette.
  2. Reorder with ↑ ↓ (top of the list is drawn last, on top). Name each layer; give it a legend.
  3. Set the start view, then use the Map card to switch layers on and off.
Map extensions
User guide B · filter at the level of each layer

Each sheet is a layer, so each layer has its own filter

Filters, dashboard actions and parameters on a layer's sheet change that layer only.

  1. On a layer's sheet, drag a field to Filters (e.g. Store format on Stores).
  2. Show the filter control on the dashboard. Its menu ▸ Apply to Worksheets ▸ Selected Worksheets ▸ tick only that layer's sheet.
  3. The Regions and Routes layers keep their own filters, unaffected.

Why it works

The extension receives, for each layer, only the rows its sheet returns. It never filters by itself, so every Tableau mechanism applies per layer.

Also per layer

  • Dashboard actions (click a region, filter only stores)
  • Context and data-source filters
  • Top N, sets, calculated fields
Map extensions
User guide B · automatic date change

A parameter that steps through the dates for all layers

One play button moves Regions, Stores and Routes through time together.

  1. Create a list parameter Period (e.g. 2019 … 2025, or month names).
  2. In each layer's sheet, create a boolean calculation such as [Year] = [Period] and put it on Filters set to True.
  3. Add the Parameter player (Extension object) to the dashboard and choose Period with the gear icon.
  1. Press ▶. Set Speed and Loop as you like.
  2. Optional: start on the latest value so the map opens on today's data.
Only layers whose sheet uses the parameter move, so you decide which layers animate and which stay fixed (for example the region fill is static while stores change).
Map extensions
Reference

Tips and current limits

 

Tips

  • A spatial field goes on Detail; the Marks tiles refuse it
  • Union several tables and use a Layer column to get several layers from one sheet
  • Globe: set Auto-rotate for kiosks and demos
  • Time line: Everything up to this step keeps track trails visible
  • Name layers clearly; legends use the layer name

Limits today

  • No click-to-select / cross-filtering from the map yet
  • Cartogram is in the worksheet version only
  • A viewer's Map card changes last for the session only
  • Very large boundary sets (postcodes, counties) not yet load-tested
  • Cloud / Server require an admin allow-list entry
